name: Ilford XP2 Super
notes: Chromogenic black-and-white film (the image is dye, formed in C-41 colour negative chemistry); the curve is a single neutral density, kind 'bw-negative' with process C-41 as instructed. Characteristic curve is on page 3: 'processed through standard C41 type chemicals', representative of 35mm and roll film.

Characteristic curve: x axis is RELATIVE log exposure (frame 0 to 4.5, no absolute lux-seconds, no Log H Ref), y is density, frame bottom = 0 (gridlines every 0.5, labelled 1.0 and 2.0). Densitometry type is not stated; balance 'daylight' is the light of the ISO 400/27 speed rating ('to daylight', measured with standard C41 processing). Traced as v; base+fog about 0.27 as read, curve starts at relative log exposure about 0.17 and ends at about 4.45 with density about 1.9 and a shoulder (the lowest top density of the Ilford sheets, the sheet's very wide latitude).
This sheet is a lower-resolution scan than the other Ilford sheets (soft lines, light jpeg noise), so values are good to about 0.02 density.

Spectral sensitivity (page 2): 'Wedge spectrogram to tungsten light (2856K)' drawn as a line curve on a 'Sensitivity' axis with ticks 0.5 and 1.0 only (frame bottom = 0 on that scale); traced as sensitivity/v with the numbers as printed (relative; linear or log not stated). The curve runs about 353-657 nm and is essentially the HP5 Plus / FP4-type panchromatic shape.

The sheet says XP2 can be exposed from EI 50 to 800 with the same processing; the curve is for a single, unstated exposure index. No document code (footer 'Page n of 5, Nov 2018'), no granularity figure.
